sentences.text: Author: K. Lakshman Bench: K. Lakshman  HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE K. LAKSHMAN  CONTEMPT CASE No.906 of 2021 ORDER:
This Contempt Case is filed alleging willful and deliberate violation of order dated 19-07-2021 in I.A.Nos.1 to 6 in W.P.No.15948 of 2021.

Vide aforesaid order, this Court gave the following directions:
"i. Respondent No.9 is directed to forthwith register and investigate into said crime in accordance with law including seizure of animals/bulls/cattle found and also illegal transportation of animals,
ii) The respondents are directed to strictly implement the directions issued by the Division Bench vide order dated 12.03.2019 in W.P.(PIL) No.203 of 2018 and Taken Up W.P.(PIL) No.10 of 2019, by considering the provisions of the above said Rules,
2001, Acts,
iii) The respondents are directed to take all precautionary measures to strictly implement the Animal Welfare Laws to stop illegal killing of animals and to take stringent action against the offenders violating the animal laws i.e., Act, 1960,
Transport of Animals Rules, 1978, Transport of Animals (Amendment) Rules, 2001,
Slaughter House Rules, 2001, Municipal Laws and Food Safety and Standards Authority of India directions for slaughtering of animals during Bakrid Festival.
iv) The respondents herein more particularly respondent Nos.1 and 2, to strictly implement the directions issued by Animal Welfare Board of India in its proceedings dated 25.06.2021.

entities.text: Municipal Laws and Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: v) The respondent Nos.2 and 10 are directed to file action taken report in the matter by 02.08.2021."
According to the petitioner, respondents have not complied with the said directions.

sentences.text: 1 In paragraph No.5 of the affidavit there is specific mention about lodging of complaint on 19-07-2021 with Police, Bahadurpura.
In view of the same, respondentNo.1 had filed counter.

It reads as under:
"a.

On the intervening night of 19/20-07-2021 at about 00:10 hours written petition was received from Sri Sumanth Ojha, Gau Gyan Foundation in which he informed that more than 100 No. of cattle have been kept/hoarded for sacrifice/Qurbani at Opp: Madina Hotel in the limits of Bahadurpura Police Station, stating that as per the order of the Hon'ble High Court of Telanana in W.P.No.15948 of 2021, no cattle can be slaughtered without fit to slaughter certificate and proper documents and requested to seize and recover cattle and early action solicited.

On receipt of the above petition, concerned police made GD Entry vide pate No.277,
para No.27 of Police Station Bahadurpura and Adll. Inspector of Police, Sri A. Shiva Kumar, ASI M.A. Kareem along with Patrol Car II PCs 8167 & 1669 of Bahadurpura Police Station went verified and the above mentioned area to check the cattle kept for illegal slaughtering.

They found one cattle seller with (06) Ox, Opposite Madina Hotel, Kishan Bagh, Hyderabad in which he produced the fitness certificate and receipt of (06) Ox and the same was informed to petitioner Sumanth Ojha.
b.

Further on the petition lodged in the Kamatipura Police Station, it is to submit that, on the Intervening night of 19/20.07.2021 at 00.30 hours received a petition from Gau Gyan Foundation represented by Sri Kamalesh Maharaj and others stating that more than 100 numbers cattle's have been kept/hoarded at Osmanbagh,
Bandlaguda, Doodhbowli, Chandulal Barari, Palam Road, Fathedarwada, etc. in the limits Kamatipura Police Station and requested to seize and recover the cattle kept hoarded for illegal slaughter.
On receipt of the above complaint, made GD Entry vide SL.No.24 and page No.240,
as there was no clarity for collecting some more evidence, immediately two teams were formed with the available force, one team was led by Sri P.Chandra Mouli, SI of Police along with Sri M. Vijay Kumar, PC 5687, Sri Ch. Srikanth, PC 9656, Sri Rukumuddin, HC 4108 and another team was led by Sri G. Srinivas, Addl. Inspector of Police along with Sri A. Ranganayakulu, HC 4659, Sri Syed Abudl Jaleel, PC 5292,
Sri N. Naveen Kumar, PC 4010.
Both the teams visited the above mentioned places and found the cattle sellers.

They caused enquiry with them and they revealed that,
the cattle's were not intended to sell for slaughtering purpose and the same statements were recorded in detail and collected the documents which were issued by the Veterinary Officer, Shabad, Ranga Reddy District.
c.

On the petition lodged in the Golconda Police Station, it is to submit that, on the intervening night of 19/20.07.2021 at 02.07 hours received a petition from Gau Gyan Foundation stating that more than 100 numbers cattle's have been kept/hoarded at M/S. Gau Gyan Foundation vs Sri.M.Mahender Reddy And 2 Others on 6 December, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121374391/
2 Chota Bazar, Bada Bazar and Fathe Darwaza in the limits of Golconda Police Station and requested to kindly seize and recover the cattle kept hoarded for illegal slaughter.

On receipt of complaint, made GD Entry vide Sl.No.16 and page No.141, as there was no clarity, for collecting some more evidence, immediately two teams were formed with the available force, one team was led by Sri J.Mahender Reddy, SI of Police and PC 5319 SP.Sai Charan, PC5549 N.Praveen and another team with Sri.K.Veera Swamy, ASI and PC5765 Bhanu Chander, PC 30779 Hruday Sagar.
The Police teams have visited the areas mentioned by the complaint at Chota Bazar, Golconda, towards which few animals were noticed by them.
The owner was called for and when enquired with the owner i.e., Mr.Basheer, told to Police team that he is the owner of these male cattle and he is a cattle trader by profession.

He also told that throughout the year he used to purchase the cattle's meant for breeding and draught purposes and he used to sell the same to the prospective farmers within and outside the state and good animals he used to rear himself also.

He further stated that on 18.07.2021 he has purchased all these 6 male cattle's which were present on the spot from new Gandhigunj agriculture market, Vikarabad District, legally after paying the market fees for the purpose of transportation of the same from Vikarabad to Golconda and he handed over the copy of receipt issued to this effect by the new Gandhigunj market, Vikarabad Agricultural Marketing Department, Govt. of Telangana.
The copy of the same is enclosed herewith.

He also told to the Police team that before transporting these male cattles he obtained a Certificate from the competent authority viz., Veterinary Assistant Surgeon, Vikarabad District, stating that the above cattles are fit for transportation from Vikarabad to Golconda, Hyderabad and meant for draught purpose.
The same is verified and copy of the same has been obtain from him which is enclosed herewith.
Having satisfied with the version of the owner of cattle's, after due verifying the documents submitted by him the police authorities have not confiscated the cattle's.

Therefore, it is evident that in all 3 cases, in which petitions were given by volunteers (Sri Sumanth Ojha, Sri Kamalesh Maharaj) of Gau Gyan Foundation, necessary action, as per law, was taken immediately by the police.
It is also noticed that complaints given by petitioner were exaggerated.
Even though few cattles are seen in photo and found accordingly on checking, they mentioned about hundreds of cattle in each petition."
Thus, according to respondent No.1 they have complied with the aforesaid order.
Petitioner did not file any reply to the said counter.

However, during the course of hearing, it is brought to the notice of this Court that respondents have already filed counters in the aforesaid writ petition and the writ petition is still pending consideration.

sentences.text: According to respondent No.1, in the counter itself they have specifically mentioned about action taken pursuant to the aforesaid interim order.
However, writ petition has to be considered basing on the pleadings of the parties.
In view of the said submissions, according to this Court, as on today there is no willful or deliberate violation of the aforesaid order passed by this Court by the respondents.
Therefore, this Contempt Case is closed.
However, liberty is granted to the petitioner to file fresh Contempt Case, if so advised on disposal of the aforesaid writ petition.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the Contempt Case shall stand closed.

K. LAKSHMAN, J December 06, 2022 PN HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE K.
